subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow stale OpenAI route/doctor repair, folded into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 as the canonical shared resolver case, or treated as expected behavior for explicit /model openai sessions with better diagnostics?
rationale: Source proves correctly selected DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the live report mixes Codex hot reload, persisted selected model state, and an explicit /model openai clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and status/runtime interpretation for non-OpenAI primaries while keeping the broader resolver issue open.

options.title: Fold into resolver tracker
options.body: Move this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 and let the shared resolver refactor own it.

options.title: Keep explicit OpenAI behavior
options.body: If the issue is only explicit /model openai selection, preserve OpenAI-to-Codex defaulting and improve status or doctor messaging instead of changing routing.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and status/runtime interpretation for non-OpenAI primaries while keeping the broader resolver issue open.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest adjacent history across session/model/status interpretation surfaces and is the best available routing owner for the product boundary choice.
